pass_b_english: It is difficult to capture the essence of the text, having been translated from its original language.
The prophets spoke in the language of the Hebrews, and Moses' words were made known, so that they would be familiar to all.
However, the multitude has been deceived by the myths of the gods and has become ignorant of the true nature of God.
Whoever is wise will praise the elegant language of the Greeks, but will not be swayed by false speech, instead speaking the truth and being of benefit to others.
For the one who speaks the truth will be useful to others, and whoever has knowledge of divine Scripture will be improved by it and will also be useful to others.
As the apostle Paul teaches, we have made the names of other gods an abomination, and we know that there is no God but one (1 Corinthians 8:4).
We believe that there is only one true God, and that idols are nothing but abominable creations.
If some people are foolish and worship idols, we have not been deceived, and we do not think that there are other gods besides the one natural and universal Creator.
When it comes to the existence of idols, those who are weak in their faith may still think that the food sacrificed to idols is somehow tainted.
But we who have a clear conscience eat such food with thanksgiving, as all food is given by the one who grants its use.
As Paul says, 'if I participate in God's grace, why should I be judged impious for something I am thankful for?' (1 Corinthians 10:30).
The fact that an idol is nothing means that an offering made to it is also nothing, and so it will not offend those who are confirmed in their faith.
If someone is weak in these matters and not yet has a healthy and strong mind, they may think that what is sacrificed to idols is truly something, not yet having a pure faith.
We abhor the names of other gods and consider them detestable.

We turn to the holy Scriptures, abandoning the writings of the Greeks, for it is in the Scriptures that the glory of truth shines forth, and we praise the careful arrangement of words and the euphonic quality that resonates within them.

In responding to the doctrines presented, we find that the Scriptures contain all manner of good documents, and it is through these that one can become full of virtue and attain the glory of right actions.
We also consider that one who judges rightly, seeing the better option, gives it to the worse, and puts it to use, for we know that 'we know that an idol is nothing in the world' (1 Corinthians 8:4).
Indeed, seeing the better option, one gives it to the worse, which, having divided, is rightly put to use.

Since he contends that we should keep the faithful away from Greek letters, as from the food of the idol-priests, let him hear us again, for we are accustomed to prohibit the faithful from the food of the idol-priests, but not from Greek letters.

If someone wants to learn from God, we abhor the name of others and consider it detestable to learn from one who is in every execration; and we say that the truth is from one, and Paul teaches that we have made the name of others an abomination, and we believe that there is no God but one, and that idols are abominable; for we know that there is no God but one, and that idols are nothing in the world (1 Corinthians 8:4).
For example, if someone pours hellebore into a golden cup or into a non-golden cup, but made of very cheap material, the value of the drink is not determined by the cup, but by its inherent quality.

He who forces labor upon others and orders them to drink from the most shameful things has learned to enslave the intellects, and may prefer the worse material, or judge it necessary to overcome the Greeks with words.

For us, however, it is no longer so, for if someone pours the honey into a golden cup or into another, not such, but rather into a very cheap one, he puts the labor of the bees into the material, then orders it to be poured out at his discretion.
Thus, seeing the better option, he gives it to the worse, which, having divided, he rightly puts to use.
Therefore, if an occasion arises, where idol offerings have been made, it will not offend those who are confirmed in faith, for if an idol is nothing, then an idol offering will be nothing.

We turn to the holy Scriptures, having abandoned Greek writings, in which the glory of truth shines, and we praise the accurate arrangement of words, and the euphonic quality, answering the doctrines in them, all kinds of good documents are contained, and every virtue, through which someone immediately becomes full and escapes, and the glory of right actions.
